LESSON: EMPHASIS INDICATORS ● RECOGNIZING AND INTERPRETING (ITALIC SIGN, BOLD)

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: GRADE
Strand: Braille Reading Skills
Topic 2.1: Emphasis indicators ● Recognizing and interpreting (Italic sign, bold)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Emphasis indicators ● Recognizing and interpreting (Italic sign, bold), part of Braille Reading Skills in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9 GRADE.

Key inquiry question: How do we write selected emphasis indicators in braille?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify common braille emphasis indicators in a braille text for learning,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Emphasis indicators ● Recognizing and interpreting (Italic sign, bold) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. explain the purpose of common braille emphasis indicators in a braille text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Emphasis indicators ● Recognizing and interpreting (Italic sign, bold) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. read texts with common braille emphasis indicators,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Emphasis indicators ● Recognizing and interpreting (Italic sign, bold) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate working with documents with common braille emphasis indicators in a braille text for reading fluency.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Emphasis indicators ● Recognizing and interpreting (Italic sign, bold) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate working with documents with common braille emphasis indicators in a braille text for reading fluency.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. interact with different braille texts with common emphasis indicators (italic sign, bold sign and underline sign) to identify and share with peers,

2. in groups brainstorm to explain uses of common braille emphasis indicators in a braille text and present their findings in plenary,

3. in pairs read aloud to one another from different pieces of braille texts provided and share experiences of encountering with common braille emphasis indicators,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. interact with different braille texts with common emphasis indicators (italic sign, bold sign and underline sign) to identify and share with peers,
2. in groups brainstorm to explain uses of common braille emphasis indicators in a braille text and present their findings in plenary,
3. in pairs read aloud to one another from different pieces of braille texts provided and share experiences of encountering with common braille emphasis indicators,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Emphasis indicators ● Recognizing and interpreting (Italic sign, bold) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-Efficacy: the learner gains confidence in fluently reading and understanding as interact with different braille texts

with common emphasis indicators to identify and share with peers.

Values:
● Respect: the learner listens and appreciates others’ views during group brainstorming on the contractions and short

forms in advanced English braille.

● Peace: the learner works harmoniously with peers when in pairs read aloud to one another from different pieces of

braille texts provided and share experiences of encountering with common braille emphasis indicators.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Life Skill Education: the learner visits a school or a nearby library to read more braille texts with common braille

indicators and write short essays about them.

2. explain the purpose of common braille emphasis indicators in a braille text,
3. read texts with common braille emphasis indicators,
4. appreciate working with documents with common braille emphasis indicators in a braille text for reading fluency.
